source_notes.label: Molecular mixing before oxide formation
source_notes.summary: The authors use a heterometallic alkoxide with Gd/Fe = 1:1 and existing Gd–O–Fe connections. They argue that atomic-scale cation mixing avoids the intermediate phases possible when separate metal salts are mixed. This is source-attributed synthesis reasoning, not an independently verified reaction mechanism.
source_locators: Main PDF p. 1–2, 4, Introduction, molecular precursor and conclusion

source_notes.label: Hydrolysis and thermal conversion
source_notes.summary: Water activation creates a sol and gel. The authors attribute the thermal-loss stages to solvent loss, removal of alkoxy groups, then dehydroxylation/condensation. A DTA exotherm around 680 °C accompanies oxide crystallization; it is an analytical signal, not an additional synthesis dwell.
source_locators: Main PDF p. 2, 5, Thermal discussion and Nanopowder Synthesis

source_notes.label: Temperature-dependent ordering and dimensions
source_notes.summary: The 600 °C powder is amorphous, 700 °C shows initial crystallization and 800 °C shows a developed orthoferrite pattern. The 45, 55 and 70 nm values are XRD crystallite estimates at 800, 1000 and 1200 °C. The approximately 60 nm faceted crystallites in TEM belong specifically to the 1000 °C specimen.
source_locators: Main PDF p. 2–3, Figures 2–3 and structural discussion

source_notes.label: Phase purity has a defined evidence scope
source_notes.summary: The diffraction discussion reports no garnet or other crystalline intermediate, and EDX reports no cation segregation at examined spots. These observations do not establish every possible impurity below detection or provide measured atomic coordinates. The molecular precursor cell in Table 1 must not be used as the oxide cell.
source_locators: Main PDF p. 2–3, 5, XRD/EDX discussion and Table 1

source_notes.label: Mixed magnetic contributions
source_notes.summary: The authors interpret the near-linear response as a dominant Gd paramagnetic contribution plus weak ferromagnetism from canting in the Fe sublattice. Their series-level coercivity and model-derived canting values are retained as context, not assigned as separate precise measurements to both calcination specimens. They report no superparamagnetic response in the examined size range.
source_locators: Main PDF p. 3–4, Figure 4 and magnetic interpretation
